overview: The final day of the 7th Annual Medford Jazz Festival featured performances by the Nico Guerrero Trio, the Berklee Institute of Jazz and Gender Justice, and the Ally Project. The event focused on the intersection of jazz, local history, and social justice while celebrating the 90th anniversary of the West Medford Community Center.

items.title: Festival Opening and Acknowledgments
items.summary: Jonathan Fagan opened the third day of the festival by thanking sponsors, technical crews, and the West Medford Community Center for hosting the event.

items.title: History of the West Medford Community Center
items.summary: Terry Carter described the 90-year history of the center as a hub for the African American community in West Medford and highlighted the historical significance of the surrounding neighborhood.

items.title: Performance: Nico Guerrero Trio
items.summary: The trio performed a set of jazz compositions influenced by Colombian rhythmic traditions, including 'Bacatá' and 'Fandango de Luna'.

items.title: Performance: Berklee Institute of Jazz and Gender Justice
items.summary: A student quartet performed a set of jazz standards written by female and non-binary composers to advocate for gender equity in the art form.

items.title: Performance: The Ally Project
items.summary: Terry Carter performed original spoken word poetry backed by a jazz trio, with pieces addressing gentrification in West Medford, the legacy of jazz icons like Duke Ellington and John Coltrane, and contemporary racial identity.

items.title: Closing Remarks
items.summary: Fagan concluded the festival with final acknowledgments of the performers and staff, inviting the audience to engage with future jam sessions and events.
